advances: Removes central symmetry from the arbitrary heterogeneous one-center product theorem. A symmetric core uses its actual number of occupied parity classes as capacity, while every remaining atom uses one disjoint parity class. An exact original-probability partition transfers one common constant through the entire product. This proves the arithmetic second- and third-moment bounds for every complete convex lattice support with at most one nontrivial integral midpoint center, and every heterogeneous product of such supports, under arbitrary affine fields. It does not cover supports with several nontrivial integral midpoint centers and does not prove the locked mixed-integer conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107 supplies the symmetric one-center scalar and multiscale mechanism and the canonical selected-row notation. Its normalization-dependent scalar estimates and final capacity conversion are proved anew above for the actual pair count M; its original theorem is not applied outside its stated ambient normalization. Accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705 supplies the canonical actual-depth and reflected definitions, the increasing concavity of \(\operatorname{arcosh}(u)^2\), and the reflection-orbit source mechanism, whose selected-row version is also verified above. No other predecessor or unaccepted result is used.
proof:
We first prove the pair-count strengthening needed from the symmetric theorem of accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107. Its ambient normalization \(K=2^n\) cannot simply be replaced in the theorem statement, because the activity test changes. We give the scalar proof and product selection under the new normalization.

Fix a finite nonempty complete convex lattice support \(A\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) that is symmetric about zero and whose only possible nontrivial integral midpoint center is zero. Let \(p_x=e^{\ell\cdot x}/Z\), where \(Z=\sum_{x\in A}e^{\ell\cdot x}\). Convexity and completeness imply \(0\in A\). Choose one representative of each nonzero antipodal pair and adjoin zero to obtain B. Set \(M=|B|\) and \(h=2M-1=|A|\). If distinct x,y have the same coordinatewise parity, their integral midpoint must be zero, so \(y=-x\). The zero parity class contains only zero, since a nonzero even x would have the nonzero integral midpoint x/2 with zero. Thus the M members of B represent exactly the M occupied parity classes, and \(M\le2^n\). Moreover the canonical reflected rows are
\(R_0=A\) and \(R_j=\lbrace j\rbrace\) for \(j\ne0\).

Throughout this scalar argument, \(H_p,b,\chi,\kappa_j,Y_j,V_j,q_j,\nu\) have precisely their meanings in accepted facts 1b91f86ed4c91107 and 445a9e668ee1a705:
$$
\begin{aligned}
H_p(j)&=\sum_{x\in R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},
&b(p)&=\sum_jp_jH_p(j)^2,
&\chi(p)&=\sum_jp_jH_p(j),\\
\kappa_j(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}}}{H_p(j)},
&Y_j(x)&=\frac12\log\frac{p_x}{p_{2j-x}},
&V_j&=\mathbb E_{\kappa_j}Y_j^2,\\
q_j&=\frac{p_jH_p(j)^2}{b(p)},
&\nu&=\sum_jq_jV_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$
The sums are oriented: both nonzero orientations occur, and the central atom occurs once. These are the full canonical quantities for the original law p. The pair-count normalized quantities are
$$
\widetilde A_0=M^2\sum_xp_x^3,\qquad
\widetilde g=\log(M^2b(p)),\qquad
\mu=\frac1M\sum_{b\in B}\cosh(\ell\cdot b),\qquad
t=\log(2\mu).
\tag{6}
$$
For the exact map to accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107, its B,M,h,\(\mu,t,p,Z,H_p,b,\chi,\kappa,Y,V,q,\nu\) are unchanged. Its \(K=2^n\), \(A_0=K^2\sum p_x^3\), and \(g=\log(K^2b(p))\) satisfy
\(\widetilde A_0=(M/K)^2A_0\) and
\(\widetilde g=g+2\log(M/K)\), where the logarithms are algebraically defined whether or not the corresponding activity condition holds. We will use the new activity condition \(\widetilde A_0<1\), with \(\widetilde d=-\log\widetilde A_0\) only in that case. No probability or unscaled reflected quantity is changed.

Put \(Z_3=\sum_{x\in A}e^{3\ell\cdot x}\). The row description gives the following identities, all with the original normalizer Z:
$$
\begin{aligned}
H_p(0)&=h/Z,& H_p(j)&=p_j\quad(j\ne0),\\
\widetilde A_0&=M^2Z_3/Z^3,
&M^2b(p)&=M^2(Z_3-1+h^2)/Z^3,\\
\kappa_0(x)&=1/h,&Y_0(x)&=\ell\cdot x,\\
V_0&=\frac2h\sum_{b\in B}(\ell\cdot b)^2,
&q_0&=\frac{h^2}{Z_3-1+h^2},\qquad \nu=q_0V_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$
Every other row is a singleton with zero score. If M=1, then A is the singleton \(\lbrace0\rbrace\), \(\widetilde A_0=1\), and \(\nu=0\). Suppose henceforth that \(\widetilde A_0<1\); in particular \(M\ge2\). Holder's inequality on the h original probabilities gives \(\sum_xp_x^3\ge h^{-2}\). Since \(M<h<2M\),
\(1/4<\widetilde A_0<1\) and \(0<\widetilde d<\log4<2\).

For the auxiliary uniform average over B, write \(a_b=\cosh(\ell\cdot b)\), the quantity denoted \(c_b\) in accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107, and
\(\mathcal V=\mathbb E_B(a_b-\mu)^2\). This average does not replace p. The identities \(\cosh(3u)=4\cosh^3u-3\cosh u\) and \(a_b\ge1\) give
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z&=2M\mu-1,\\
Z_3&=8M\mathbb E_Ba_b^3-6M\mu-1,\\
\mathbb E_Ba_b^3-\mu^3
&=\mathbb E_B[(a_b-\mu)^2(a_b+2\mu)]\ge2\mu\mathcal V.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$
Activity therefore implies
$$
M^2(8M\mu^3+16M\mu\mathcal V-6M\mu-1)
\le M^2Z_3<Z^3<(2M\mu)^3,
$$
whence \(\mathcal V<3/8+1/(16M\mu)\le7/16<1\). The term at \(b=0\) implies \((\mu-1)^2/M\le\mathcal V<1\). Thus \(\mu<\sqrt M+1\le2\sqrt M\), and \(\mu^2<4M\).

Jensen gives \(\mathbb E_Ba_b^3\ge\mu^3\). Since \(8M\mu^3-6M\mu-1>0\), (7)-(8) and \(Z<2M\mu\) imply
$$
\widetilde A_0>
1-\frac3{4\mu^2}-\frac1{8M\mu^3}
\ge1-\frac7{8\mu^2}.
\tag{9}
$$
Define the auxiliary increment \(E=M^2(h^2-1)/Z^3\), so \(M^2b(p)=\widetilde A_0+E\). Since \(h^2-1=4M(M-1)\ge2M^2\) and \(\mu^2<4M\),
$$
E>\frac M{4\mu^3}>\frac1{16\mu}.
\tag{10}
$$
The increasing concavity of \(u\mapsto\operatorname{arcosh}(u)^2\) on \([1,\infty)\) is proved in accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705. Apply it to the uniform average over B. Because \(2M/h\le4/3\) and \(\operatorname{arcosh}\mu\le\log(2\mu)=t\),
$$
V_0=\frac{2M}{h}\mathbb E_B(\ell\cdot b)^2
\le\frac43\operatorname{arcosh}(\mu)^2\le\frac43t^2.
\tag{11}
$$
This includes \(\mu=1\), when every score is zero.

We next verify a positive logarithmic energy under the pair-count normalization. Completeness and affinity give the exact midpoint identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
\chi(p)
&=\sum_{\substack{x,y\in A\\x\equiv y\pmod2}}
 p_{(x+y)/2}\sqrt{p_xp_y}\\
&=\sum_{\rho\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^n}p(\rho+2\mathbb Z^n)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
$$
Indeed the midpoint is in A, and \(p_{(x+y)/2}=\sqrt{p_xp_y}\) with the original Z. There are exactly M occupied parity classes. The zero class has mass \(p_0=1/Z\le1/h<1/M\). Cauchy--Schwarz on the other M-1 classes gives
\(\chi(p)\ge p_0^2+(1-p_0)^2/(M-1)\). The right side decreases for \(p_0\in[0,1/M]\), and its value at \(1/h\) is \((4M-3)/h^2\). Consequently
$$
M\chi(p)\ge\frac{M(4M-3)}{h^2}
=1+\frac{M-1}{h^2}\ge1+\frac1{8M}.
$$
Jensen under the entire original p gives \(b(p)\ge\chi(p)^2\). Since \(2\log(1+u)\ge u\) for \(0\le u\le1\),
$$
\widetilde g\ge2\log\left(1+\frac1{8M}\right)
\ge\frac1{8M}>0.
\tag{13}
$$

If \(\mu\ge64\), let \(\delta=1-\widetilde A_0\). By (9)-(10),
\(0<\delta<7/(8\mu^2)\le E/4\). Thus
\(M^2b(p)=1-\delta+E\ge1+3E/4>1+3/(64\mu)\).
The inequality \(\log(1+u)\ge u/(1+u)\) gives
\(\widetilde g\ge1/(32\mu)\). Also (9) and
\(-\log(1-u)\le2u\) for \(0\le u\le1/2\) give
\(\widetilde d\le2/\mu^2\). Hence
\(\widetilde d\le(64/\mu)\widetilde g=128e^{-t}\widetilde g\).
Furthermore (7) gives
$$
q_0=\frac{h^2}{h^2-1}\frac E{M^2b(p)}
\le\frac98\frac E{M^2b(p)}
\le\frac32\frac{M^2b(p)-1}{M^2b(p)}
\le\frac32\widetilde g.
\tag{14}
$$
Here \(h\ge3\), \(M^2b(p)-1\ge3E/4\), and
\(1-u^{-1}\le\log u\) for \(u\ge1\) justify the three inequalities. Together with (11), this gives \(\nu\le2t^2\widetilde g\).

If \(1\le\mu<64\), then \(e^{-t}>2^{-7}\). Since \(Z_3\ge1\), \(h>M\), and \(Z<2M\mu\), (7) gives
$$
M^2b(p)\ge\frac{M^2h^2}{Z^3}>\frac M{8\mu^3}.
\tag{15}
$$
If \(M\ge2^{22}=16\cdot64^3\), (15) implies \(\widetilde g>\log2>1/2\). Using \(\widetilde d<2\), (11), and \(q_0\le1\), we obtain
\(\widetilde d/(e^{-t}\widetilde g)<2^9\) and
\(\nu/(t^2\widetilde g)<8/3\).
If \(M<2^{22}\), (13) gives \(\widetilde g>2^{-25}\), so the corresponding bounds are \(2^{33}\) and \((4/3)2^{25}<2^{26}\). Since \(t\ge\log2>0\), every division is valid. We have therefore proved, under the new activity condition, with \(C=2^{40}\),
$$
\widetilde g>0,\qquad
\widetilde d\le Ce^{-t}\widetilde g,\qquad
\nu\le Ct^2\widetilde g.
\tag{16}
$$
This accounts for the normalization change in every scalar estimate (4)-(17) of accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107. The original uses of K there were the bound \(M\le K\), the active-case implications \(h>K\) and \(K\ge2\), the collision-energy lower bound, the small-\(\mu\) threshold, and the factors \(K^2\) in the definitions. Under \(K=M\), the active case gives \(M\ge2\) and \(h>M\), and all those bounds have just been established directly. In particular (13) counts the actual M parity classes and does not presume that M is a power of two.

We next prove that (16) yields one common coefficient for any finite product of these symmetric supports. For this intermediate assertion consider \(\Pi=\bigotimes_i\pi_i\), where \(\pi_i\) is an arbitrary affine law on a centered symmetric one-center complete convex lattice support \(S_i\), and let \(m_i=(|S_i|+1)/2\). The exact alias map to the preceding scalar argument is \(p=\pi_i,A=S_i,M=m_i\); all indexed reflected quantities from (5) are evaluated for \(\pi_i\). The alias map to the product notation of accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107 is \(p_i=\pi_i,P=\Pi\). The original possibly asymmetric laws (1) are not changed. A factor is active when
\(\widetilde A_{0,i}=m_i^2\sum_x\pi_{i,x}^3<1\). An inactive factor will use singleton auxiliary rows at every center. These have scaled energy \(\widetilde A_{0,i}\ge1\) and zero price, including when \(m_i=1\).

For each active factor use \(t_i,\widetilde d_i,\widetilde g_i,\nu_i\) from (16). For integers \(m\ge0\), set
$$
I_m=\lbrace i:\widetilde A_{0,i}<1,\ m\le t_i<m+1\rbrace,
\qquad G_m=\sum_{i\in I_m}\widetilde g_i.
$$
All active factors lie in these bins. If \(G_m\ge4C(m+1)^2\), use full canonical rows in every factor of \(I_m\). Its total price \(T_m=\sum_{i\in I_m}\nu_i\) then satisfies
\(T_m\le C(m+1)^2G_m\le G_m^2/4\), hence \(G_m\ge2\sqrt{T_m}\).
Otherwise use singleton rows in every factor of \(I_m\). The lost logarithmic energy is at most
$$
\sum_{i\in I_m}\widetilde d_i
\le Ce^{-m}G_m<4C^2e^{-m}(m+1)^2.
\tag{17}
$$
Empty bins contribute zero. Since
\(\sum_{m\ge0}(m+1)^2r^m=(1+r)/(1-r)^3\) and \(e^{-1}<1/2\), the total of the right sides is less than \(D=48C^2\).

We verify the selected-row source with no normalization depending on an ambient dimension. Write \(\widehat R_{i,j}\) for the selected row, which is either the full \(R_{i,j}\) or \(\lbrace j\rbrace\). Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat H_i(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_{i,j}}\sqrt{\pi_{i,x}\pi_{i,2j-x}},
&\widehat b_i&=\sum_j\pi_{i,j}\widehat H_i(j)^2,\\
\widehat\kappa_{i,j}(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{\pi_{i,x}\pi_{i,2j-x}}}{\widehat H_i(j)},
&\widehat q_{i,j}&=\frac{\pi_{i,j}\widehat H_i(j)^2}{\widehat b_i},\\
\widehat V_{i,j}&=\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_{i,j}}Y_{i,j}^2,
&\widehat\nu_i&=\sum_j\widehat q_{i,j}\widehat V_{i,j},
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$
where \(Y_{i,j}(x)=\frac12\log(\pi_{i,x}/\pi_{i,2j-x})\) remains the canonical score. These are exactly the selected-row objects in (21) of accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107. A full factor contributes logarithmic scaled energy \(\widetilde g_i\) and price \(\nu_i\); a singleton-selected factor has \(\widehat H_i(j)=\pi_{i,j}\), scaled energy \(\widetilde A_{0,i}\), and price zero. Thus, with \(S_g=\sum_i\log(m_i^2\widehat b_i)\), (17) and the nonnegative inactive energies give
$$
S_g\ge\sum_{m:\,G_m\ge4C(m+1)^2}G_m-D
\ge2\sum_{m:\,G_m\ge4C(m+1)^2}\sqrt{T_m}-D
\ge2\sqrt{\sum_i\widehat\nu_i}-D.
\tag{19}
$$
The last inequality follows by squaring the nonnegative sum of square roots, and includes an empty sum.

For a supported \(J=(j_i)\), let \(\widehat R_J=\prod_i\widehat R_{i,j_i}\), \(\widehat H_\Pi(J)=\prod_i\widehat H_i(j_i)\), and \(\widehat\kappa_J=\bigotimes_i\widehat\kappa_{i,j_i}\). Put \(Y_J(X)=\sum_iY_{i,j_i}(x_i)\) and \(\sigma_J^2=\sum_i\widehat V_{i,j_i}\). Reflection preserves each selected row and its auxiliary law, and reverses its score. Independence and direct substitution therefore give
$$
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J=0,\qquad
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J^2=\sigma_J^2,\qquad
\Pi_X=\widehat H_\Pi(J)\widehat\kappa_J(X)e^{Y_J(X)}
\quad(X\in\widehat R_J).
\tag{20}
$$
The law \(\Pi\) in this symmetric-product assertion is the full product of its factor laws; in particular \(\Pi_X=\prod_i\pi_{i,x_i}\) with every defining factor normalizer intact. Any ambient closed halfspace containing J contains at least one member of each distinct reflected pair \(X,2J-X\) and also contains J. The reflection-orbit argument of (25) in accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705, or its direct sum over these selected orbits, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_\Pi(J)
&\ge\frac12\sum_{X\in\widehat R_J}\min\lbrace \Pi_X,\Pi_{2J-X}\rbrace\\
&=\frac{\widehat H_\Pi(J)}2\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}e^{-|Y_J|}
\ge\frac{\widehat H_\Pi(J)}2e^{-\sigma_J}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
$$
The factor 1/2 cancels the two orientations on every noncentral orbit and uses at most half the central mass. Jensen for \(e^{-u}\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, proves the last inequality. This argument applies to all ambient containing halfspaces regardless of affine rank.

For \(\widehat q=\bigotimes_i\widehat q_i\), the factorization
\(\Pi_J\widehat H_\Pi(J)^2=(\prod_i\widehat b_i)\prod_i\widehat q_{i,j_i}\) is exact, and \(\mathbb E_{\widehat q}\sigma_J^2=\sum_i\widehat\nu_i\). Squaring (21), averaging against the entire \(\Pi\), and using Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$$
M_2(\Pi)\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)
\mathbb E_{\widehat q}e^{-2\sigma_J}
\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)
\exp\left(-2\sqrt{\sum_i\widehat\nu_i}\right).
\tag{22}
$$
This is the scale-free selected source in (26) of accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107, also verified here. Combining (19) and (22) proves the pair-count product bound
$$
M_2(\Pi)\ge\frac{e^{-D}}{4\prod_im_i^2}
=c_*\left(\prod_im_i\right)^{-2}.
\tag{23}
$$
Jensen under \(\Pi\) gives \(M_3(\Pi)\ge M_2(\Pi)^{3/2}\). The only final use of \(K_i=2^{n_i}\) in the accepted proof was the identity \(\prod_iK_i^2=4^N\); (23) instead retains \(\prod_im_i^2\). The constant is unchanged because \(D=48C^2=48\cdot2^{80}\). This proves the claimed strengthening for every symmetric product, including singleton factors and no active factors. Translating each factor by any integral center preserves this conclusion: the translation bijects ambient containing closed halfspaces, and the translated affine law has the same field and its exact translated normalizer.

Return now to the original, possibly asymmetric supports and laws (1). If \(\mathcal C_i\) is nonempty, its member \(c_i=(x+y)/2\) lies in Q_i by convexity and is integral, so \(c_i\in A_i\); otherwise this holds by our choice. The core R_i in (3) is nonempty, is symmetric about c_i, and is a complete convex lattice support because
$$
R_i=\bigl(Q_i\cap(2c_i-Q_i)\bigr)\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}.
\tag{24}
$$
Every nontrivial integral midpoint in R_i is also one in A_i, so it equals c_i. In the case \(\mathcal C_i=\varnothing\), the core is the singleton \(\lbrace c_i\rbrace\), since any other x in R_i would form the nontrivial integral midpoint c_i with \(2c_i-x\). In every case, translation by \(-c_i\) puts R_i under the symmetric hypotheses already proved, and \(|R_i|=2M_i-1\).

For the parity budget, suppose \(x\in A_i\setminus R_i\) had a different point \(y\in A_i\) of its parity. Its midpoint is integral, so \(\mathcal C_i\) is nonempty and \((x+y)/2=c_i\). This says \(y=2c_i-x\in A_i\), contradicting \(x\notin R_i\). Therefore every point outside R_i is the sole member of its parity class in the entire A_i. These s_i classes are distinct from one another and from every class occupied by the core. As proved in the symmetric argument after translation, the core occupies exactly M_i parity classes. Translation merely permutes parity classes. Hence
\(M_i+s_i\le2^{n_i}\), and multiplying gives \(\mathcal K\le2^N\).

Partition A_i into the core and the individual outside atoms:
\(\mathcal D_i=\lbrace R_i\rbrace\cup\lbrace\lbrace a\rbrace:a\in A_i\setminus R_i\rbrace\).
For \(D\in\mathcal D_i\), define its original mass and its exact conditional normalizer by
$$
\beta_{i,D}=\sum_{x\in D}p_{i,x}=\frac{Z_{i,D}}{Z_i},\qquad
Z_{i,D}=\sum_{x\in D}e^{\ell_i\cdot x},\qquad
p_{i,D}(x)=\frac{p_{i,x}}{\beta_{i,D}}
=\frac{e^{\ell_i\cdot x}}{Z_{i,D}}\quad(x\in D).
\tag{25}
$$
Every piece is nonempty, so all these masses are positive. When D=R_i and \(x=c_i+u\), its translated conditional law is exactly
\(e^{\ell_i\cdot u}/\overline Z_{i,R_i}\), where
\(\overline Z_{i,R_i}=e^{-\ell_i\cdot c_i}Z_{i,R_i}\). Thus the conditional law on the core retains the entire original affine field. Singleton pieces have deterministic conditional laws.

A leaf \(\lambda=(D_1,\ldots,D_L)\in\prod_i\mathcal D_i\) has support \(A_\lambda=\prod_iD_i\), original mass \(\alpha_\lambda=\prod_i\beta_{i,D_i}\), and conditional law
$$
P_\lambda(X)=\prod_ip_{i,D_i}(x_i)
=\frac{\prod_ie^{\ell_i\cdot x_i}}{\prod_iZ_{i,D_i}}
=\frac{P_X}{\alpha_\lambda}\quad(X\in A_\lambda).
\tag{26}
$$
The leaves partition the full product support and \(\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda=1\). Assign a core piece capacity \(k_{i,R_i}=M_i\) and each singleton outside piece capacity \(k_{i,\lbrace a\rbrace}=1\). Let \(k_\lambda=\prod_i k_{i,D_i}\). Translation of every chosen piece to its symmetry center turns each leaf into a product covered by (23), keeping all original conditional normalizers as in (25)-(26). The translations act on the full ambient space, so depths for P_\lambda are measured against exactly the ambient closed halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^N\). Consequently
\(M_2(P_\lambda)\ge c_*k_\lambda^{-2}\). This includes leaves consisting entirely of singletons. The capacities satisfy the exact sum identity
$$
\sum_\lambda k_\lambda
=\prod_i\left(\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_i}k_{i,D}\right)
=\prod_i(M_i+s_i)=\mathcal K.
\tag{27}
$$

For every J in a leaf and every ambient closed halfspace \(\mathcal H\) containing J, the original full law satisfies \(P(\mathcal H)\ge\alpha_\lambda P_\lambda(\mathcal H)\). Taking the infimum over that same set of halfspaces gives
\(\tau_P(J)\ge\alpha_\lambda\tau_{P_\lambda}(J)\). Averaging over every original atom therefore yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)
&\ge\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda^3M_2(P_\lambda)\\
&\ge c_*\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2}
\ge c_*\left(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\right)^{-2}
=c_*\mathcal K^{-2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
$$
For the last inequality, Holder with exponents 3 and 3/2 gives
$$
1=\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda}{k_\lambda^{2/3}}k_\lambda^{2/3}
\le\left(\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2}\right)^{1/3}
\left(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\right)^{2/3}.
$$
Thus the constant c_* is paid once for the whole partition; no factorwise multiplication of coefficients occurs. Finally Jensen for \(u^{3/2}\) under the entire original P gives
\(M_3(P)=\mathbb E_P(\tau_P^2)^{3/2}\ge M_2(P)^{3/2}\). Together with \(\mathcal K\le2^N\), this proves (4).

For completeness of the final product census, convexity gives \(\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\subseteq Q_i\), hence \(\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}=A_i\). The convex hull of a finite Cartesian product is the product of its factor convex hulls: one inclusion follows by convexity, and the other by multiplying the finite convex-combination coefficients in the factors. Intersecting this identity with \(\mathbb Z^N\) gives exactly \(\prod_iA_i\). No argument above assumes positive affine rank, deletes boundary mass, or restricts the ambient containing halfspaces.
statement:
Let \(L\ge1\) and \(n_1,\ldots,n_L\ge1\) be integers. For each i let \(Q_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be convex and let \(A_i=Q_i\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose that the set
$$
\mathcal C_i=\left\lbrace\frac{x+y}{2}:x,y\in A_i,\ x\ne y,\ \frac{x+y}{2}\in\mathbb Z^{n_i}\right\rbrace
$$
has cardinality at most one. No central symmetry, full-dimensionality, or coordinate bound is assumed. For arbitrary \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), retain the entire original laws and normalizers
$$
Z_i=\sum_{x\in A_i}e^{\ell_i\cdot x},\qquad
p_{i,x}=\frac{e^{\ell_i\cdot x}}{Z_i},\qquad
P=\bigotimes_{i=1}^Lp_i,\qquad N=\sum_{i=1}^Ln_i.
\tag{1}
$$
Extend each law by zero off its support. In the actual-depth notation of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705, put
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_P(J)&=\inf\left\lbrace P(\mathcal H):\mathcal H\subseteq\mathbb R^N
\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }J\right\rbrace,\\
M_2(P)&=\sum_JP_J\tau_P(J)^2,
& M_3(P)&=\sum_JP_J\tau_P(J)^3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$
If \(\mathcal C_i\) is nonempty, let \(c_i\) be its unique member; otherwise choose any \(c_i\in A_i\). Define the symmetric core and its capacity by
$$
R_i=A_i\cap(2c_i-A_i),\qquad
M_i=\frac{|R_i|+1}{2},\qquad
s_i=|A_i\setminus R_i|,\qquad
\mathcal K=\prod_{i=1}^L(M_i+s_i).
\tag{3}
$$
Then \(c_i\in A_i\), each \(M_i\) is a positive integer, and \(\mathcal K\le2^N\). With the same absolute constant as accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107,
\(c_* =\frac14\exp(-48\cdot2^{80})\), one has the stronger bounds
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)&\ge c_*\mathcal K^{-2}\ge c_*4^{-N},\\
M_3(P)&\ge c_*^{3/2}\mathcal K^{-3}\ge c_*^{3/2}8^{-N}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$
The product support is its complete convex lattice census. All halfspaces in (2) are ambient halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^N\), including when the product support has lower affine rank or is a singleton.
